Superseded by [#44241](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44241) after renaming the source branch to `dsv41-weight-cache-recovery`. The implementation commit is unchanged.

## Motivation

This PR extends the existing Weight Cache Daemon feature introduced in
[#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139) and described in
[Fast Engine Recovery: Sub-Second Engine Restart for SGLang via Weight Cache Daemon](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)
to DeepSeek V4.1, with Engram in either GPU or host memory.

The article addresses the repeated checkpoint I/O and weight processing paid on
every engine restart, which prolong service outages during worker failures and
rolling updates. It retains processed weights in a persistent daemon and lets
replacement engines reuse them through CUDA IPC. This PR builds on that feature
and addresses the gaps that prevent the same recovery path from working for V4.1.

**Why this extension is needed:**

- **V4.1 needs more than tensor import.** Its FP8 dense / FP4 expert path has
  post-load layouts, quantization metadata and cached tensor references that a
  replacement engine must restore consistently. Related failures are documented
  in [#39794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39794). This PR restores
  the processed state, rebinds mHC and TopK references, and checks backend/layout
  compatibility instead of merely relaxing the IPC admission check or repeating
  transforms on shared weights.
- **Host Engram needs its own resident recovery path.** GPU tensor IPC cannot
  share its host backing. This PR preserves daemon-owned host tables and imports
  them in replacement workers; optional HOST_NUMA VMM reuses allocation handles
  to avoid repeated `cudaHostRegister` on unchanged tables.
- **Faster checkpoint reads still pay checkpoint I/O on restart.** The
  InstantTensor and positioned-read PRs below accelerate loading from storage.
  This PR complements them by reusing already processed GPU weights and host
  Engram after a worker restart, while the daemon survives. Their cold-load
  optimizations can still benefit initial daemon startup, but are not included
  in this patch.

The result is a V4.1-specific implementation of the article's resident-weight
recovery path, plus an experimental prewarmed standby for its active-standby
scenario. Complete weight reload and service recovery results are reported below;
full long-context acceptance and other remaining gates are still pending.

### Related work

- [#27139 — Support fast engine recovery through weight cache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139): the original feature this PR extends.
- [#38306 — Support post-load lifecycle and MXFP4 IPC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38306): related model-support work describing K3/DSV3 validation; this PR adds V4.1-specific state restoration and host Engram recovery.
- [#39794 — Reject routed MXFP4 experts for IPC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39794): documents why accepting a base FP8 configuration is insufficient for routed-expert post-load layouts.
- [#40453 — Add InstantTensor loader support](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40453), and [#42919 — Load V4.1 with the Engram host table](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42919): accelerate checkpoint loading while keeping host-resident tables off the GPU stream.
- [#42920 — Parallel positioned reads for Engram host tables](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42920): accelerates storage-to-host loading with parallel `preadv`; this PR addresses resident recovery and mapping reuse instead.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Engram in GPU memory

Disk reload compared with resident CUDA IPC recovery:

| Metric | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Complete main-model weight reload | **50.56 s** | **1.02 s** | **49.6×** |
| Complete service recovery: process launch → healthy service | **95.09 s** | **36.53 s** | **2.60×** |

Values are medians: two final matched disk runs and three recovery runs.
Compilation/autotuning caches were warm. The weight reload covers the entire
main model, including Engram and post-load state; service recovery also includes
communication, KV and runtime initialization.

### Engram in shared host memory

| Host layout and comparison | Metric | Before | After | Speedup |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Shared table: disk reload → resident IPC + memfd | Complete main-model weight reload | **85.45 s** | **14.44 s** | **5.9×** |
| Per-rank shards: existing memfd recovery → HOST_NUMA VMM | Complete main-model weight reload | **4.77 s** | **3.36 s** | **1.42×** |
| Per-rank shards: existing memfd recovery → HOST_NUMA VMM | Launch-helper return → polled service readiness | **45.54 s** | **40.53 s** | **1.12×** |

Host recovery values are medians of three runs; the shared-table disk baseline
has one sample. Shared tables and per-rank shards are separate experiments:
85.45 s is not a matched baseline for 3.36 s. Exact process-launch to healthy
service time was not measured for the host VMM comparison; its readiness timer
starts after the launch helper returns.

Both placements require an already loaded, surviving daemon for optimized
recovery; initial daemon startup is excluded.

An already prewarmed standby provided its first response token **0.205–0.422 s after active-launcher SIGKILL** in the memfd experiment. This is standby takeover, not a new worker reload. VMM plus standby has not yet had a combined full-model fault-injection run.

**Setup:** four NVIDIA L20D GPUs, TP4/EP1/attention-DP1, native FP8 dense/FP4 expert, `flashinfer_mxfp4` / `dsv4`, vision disabled, context 4096, maximum four requests, CUDA Graph and overlap disabled. The VMM experiment used private KV capacity 8192 per worker.

## Modifications

- Add explicit V4.1 recovery opt-in, a versioned post-load state contract and compatibility fingerprint. Restore processed tensor aliases, quantization metadata, mHC references and TopK correction bias without transforming shared weights again.
- Add daemon-owned host Engram FD sharing, with `memfd` and optional `cuda_vmm` backends. VMM clients map GPU views of the same physical host allocation without copying it or repeating host registration.
- Align daemon/client backend initialization and isolate draft loading from target IPC loading.
- Add an experimental two-worker standby gateway with generation warmup, promotion and replenishment. Failed requests are not replayed, and session state is rejected.
- Add registered CPU tests and [configuration/usage documentation](https://github.com/number-eleven11/sglang/blob/codex/dsv41-weight-cache-recovery/python/sglang/srt/weight_cache/README.md).

## Accuracy Tests

**71 CPU tests pass**, and upstream lint passes. GPU measurements predate formatting/documentation edits; there were no non-import AST changes when formatting the tested implementation.

For the host VMM comparison, all 30 prompt comparisons matched text and input/output token IDs; 24/30 also matched logprobs exactly. The 1401-token prompt differed even in a memfd same-service repeat, so **strict long-context numerical acceptance remains unresolved**. Short prompts and the 385-token case were exact. Host gather and shared-table CUDA Graph component checks passed; full-model CUDA Graph/shared-layout validation is pending.

## Limitations

This remains a draft. The experiment used sglang-kernel 0.4.7 with the source's expected 0.4.9 version check bypassed; aligned-dependency validation is pending. Full-capacity throughput, draft/speculative execution and other topologies remain unvalidated. The daemon must survive, and same-GPU standby workers do not isolate GPU faults. In-flight requests/KV state are not recovered. Initial daemon host allocation costs remain; this does not implement #42920's parallel checkpoint reads.

## Checklist

- [x] Format changed code and pass upstream lint.
- [x] Add registered tests and pass 71 related CPU cases.
- [x] Document configuration and before/after recovery results.
- [ ] Complete long-context and aligned-dependency validation.
- [ ] Run full GPU CI; currently blocked by the repository's draft gate.

+# Experimental DeepSeek V4.1 recovery
+
+This extension extends the existing Weight Cache Daemon feature introduced in
+[#27139](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139) and described in
+[Fast Engine Recovery: Sub-Second Engine Restart for SGLang via Weight Cache Daemon](https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-08-21-sglang-fast-recovery)
+to DeepSeek V4.1, with Engram in either GPU or host memory.
+
+The article addresses the repeated checkpoint I/O and weight processing paid on
+every engine restart, which prolong service outages during worker failures and
+rolling updates. It retains processed weights in a persistent daemon and lets
+replacement engines reuse them through CUDA IPC. This extension builds on that feature
+and addresses the gaps that prevent the same recovery path from working for V4.1.
+
+**Why this extension is needed:**
+
+- **V4.1 needs more than tensor import.** Its FP8 dense / FP4 expert path has
+  post-load layouts, quantization metadata and cached tensor references that a
+  replacement engine must restore consistently. Related failures are documented
+  in [#39794](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39794). This extension restores
+  the processed state, rebinds mHC and TopK references, and checks backend/layout
+  compatibility instead of merely relaxing the IPC admission check or repeating
+  transforms on shared weights.
+- **Host Engram needs its own resident recovery path.** GPU tensor IPC cannot
+  share its host backing. This extension preserves daemon-owned host tables and imports
+  them in replacement workers; optional HOST_NUMA VMM reuses allocation handles
+  to avoid repeated `cudaHostRegister` on unchanged tables.
+- **Faster checkpoint reads still pay checkpoint I/O on restart.** The
+  InstantTensor and positioned-read PRs below accelerate loading from storage.
+  This extension complements them by reusing already processed GPU weights and host
+  Engram after a worker restart, while the daemon survives. Their cold-load
+  optimizations can still benefit initial daemon startup, but are not included
+  in this patch.
+
+The result is a V4.1-specific implementation of the article's resident-weight
+recovery path, plus an experimental prewarmed standby for its active-standby
+scenario. Complete weight reload and service recovery results are reported below;
+full long-context acceptance and other remaining gates are still pending.
+
+### Related work
+
+- [#27139 — Support fast engine recovery through weight cache](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/27139): the original feature this extension extends.
+- [#38306 — Support post-load lifecycle and MXFP4 IPC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/38306): related model-support work describing K3/DSV3 validation; this extension adds V4.1-specific state restoration and host Engram recovery.
+- [#39794 — Reject routed MXFP4 experts for IPC](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39794): documents why accepting a base FP8 configuration is insufficient for routed-expert post-load layouts.
+- [#40453 — Add InstantTensor loader support](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40453), and [#42919 — Load V4.1 with the Engram host table](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42919): accelerate checkpoint loading while keeping host-resident tables off the GPU stream.
+- [#42920 — Parallel positioned reads for Engram host tables](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42920): accelerates storage-to-host loading with parallel `preadv`; this extension addresses resident recovery and mapping reuse instead.
+
+## Host Engram configuration
+
+Use Linux/NVIDIA CUDA with the repository's supported dependencies. The optional
+`cuda_vmm` backend additionally requires `cuda.bindings.driver`, device support
+for HOST_NUMA VMM and POSIX FD export/import. Unsupported devices fail explicitly.
+
+Set the same environment, checkpoint, source, backend choices, and model overrides
+in the daemon and every client. For example, for a local TP4/EP1 deployment:
+
+```bash
+export MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
+export SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1
+export SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank
+
+common=(
+  --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" --trust-remote-code
+  --tp 4 --attn-dp-size 1 --ep-size 1
+  --moe-a2a-backend none --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4
+  --attention-backend dsv4
+  --json-model-override-args '{"vision_n_layers":0}'
+  --model-loader-extra-config '{"dsv41_weight_cache":true,"dsv41_host_table_backend":"cuda_vmm"}'
+  --context-length 4096 --max-total-tokens 8192 --max-running-requests 4
+  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 --max-prefill-tokens 4096
+  --mem-fraction-static 0.65 --random-seed 42
+  --disable-cuda-graph --disable-prefill-cuda-graph --disable-overlap-schedule
+)
+# Terminal 1: load and retain the processed model.
+python -m sglang.srt.weight_cache.daemon "${common[@]}"
+# Terminal 2: import resident weights; wait for the daemon to be ready first.
+python -m sglang.launch_server "${common[@]}" \
+  --weight-cache-mode client --host 127.0.0.1 --port 22941 --nccl-port 22942
+```
+
+These commands describe the tested configuration; capacity and backend support
+must be checked for your hardware. Omit the host-table environment settings for
+GPU-resident Engram. Select `"dsv41_host_table_backend":"memfd"` for the comparison
+backend. The opt-in `dsv41_weight_cache` flag is required for V4.1 IPC recovery.
+
+VMM allocates NUMA host storage once in the daemon, exports its allocation FD,
+and imports it in each worker. Clients expose a CUDA tensor alias to physical
+host memory without copying the table or calling `cudaHostRegister` again. Each
+process still pays for its own GPU access mapping. CPU checkpoint loading and
+initial allocation remain cold-start costs.
+
+The post-load manifest restores tensor aliases, cached tensor references,
+quantization flags, mHC seams and TopK correction bias references. The contract
+and layout fingerprint reject incompatible backend/configuration/source choices.
+Host descriptors validate logical size, padded allocation size, NUMA placement,
+and tensor bounds. Host-table objects own imported mappings, CUDA handles and
+FDs; retire tensor/kernel users before closing these objects.
+
+## Prewarmed standby workers
+
+`python -m sglang.srt.weight_cache.standby --config config.json` manages two
+independent client process groups. A worker becomes ready only after HTTP health
+and a generation warmup. It promotes an already ready worker after active-worker
+failure and replenishes the failed worker in the background. Manage the weight
+daemon separately.
+
+A configuration has two `workers`, each with a distinct `name`, loopback HTTP
+`url`, and a `command` argument list that launches its client server. Optional
+worker `env` entries extend the inherited environment. Use distinct HTTP/NCCL
+ports and budget both workers' private KV pools. Other settings include `host`,
+`port`, `log_dir`, `warmup`, `health_path`, `health_interval`, `health_timeout`,
+`poll_interval`, `startup_timeout`, `warmup_timeout`, and `restart_backoff`.
+Inspect `/recovery/status` for readiness and promotion events.
+
+Only stateless generation/OpenAI inference routes and model metadata are exposed.
+Requests containing `session_params` are rejected. Failed requests are never
+replayed; truncated streams are closed. HTTP health does not prove GPU forward
+progress. Two workers sharing the same GPU do not isolate device failures, and
+only one worker remains available while the standby is rebuilding.
+
+## Validation and limitations
+
+The experiment used four NVIDIA L20D GPUs, TP4/EP1/attention-DP1,
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash native FP8 dense/FP4 expert weights, context 4096 and a maximum
+of four requests. CUDA Graph and overlap were disabled.
+
+### Engram in GPU memory
+
+Disk reload compared with resident CUDA IPC recovery:
+
+| Metric | Before | After | Speedup |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Complete main-model weight reload | **50.56 s** | **1.02 s** | **49.6×** |
+| Complete service recovery: process launch → healthy service | **95.09 s** | **36.53 s** | **2.60×** |
+
+Values are medians: two final matched disk runs and three recovery runs.
+Compilation/autotuning caches were warm. The weight reload covers the entire
+main model, including Engram and post-load state; service recovery also includes
+communication, KV and runtime initialization.
+
+### Engram in shared host memory
+
+| Host layout and comparison | Metric | Before | After | Speedup |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| Shared table: disk reload → resident IPC + memfd | Complete main-model weight reload | **85.45 s** | **14.44 s** | **5.9×** |
+| Per-rank shards: existing memfd recovery → HOST_NUMA VMM | Complete main-model weight reload | **4.77 s** | **3.36 s** | **1.42×** |
+| Per-rank shards: existing memfd recovery → HOST_NUMA VMM | Launch-helper return → polled service readiness | **45.54 s** | **40.53 s** | **1.12×** |
+
+Host recovery values are medians of three runs; the shared-table disk baseline
+has one sample. Shared tables and per-rank shards are separate experiments:
+85.45 s is not a matched baseline for 3.36 s. Exact process-launch to healthy
+service time was not measured for the host VMM comparison; its readiness timer
+starts after the launch helper returns.
+
+Both placements require an already loaded, surviving daemon for optimized
+recovery; initial daemon startup is excluded.
+
+Across 30 prompt comparisons, all text and input/output token IDs matched.
+24/30 also matched logprobs exactly. The 1401-token case differed even in a memfd
+same-service repeat; strict long-context numerical acceptance remains unresolved.
+8/51/203 GB allocation probes matched an independent CPU gather oracle. Four-rank
+shared-table gather and CUDA Graph replay passed at component scope only; full
+model shared layout and full model CUDA Graphs were not validated.
+
+Earlier memfd standby fault injection measured 205–422 ms from launcher SIGKILL
+to the first response token. This is takeover by an already warmed worker, not
+VMM worker reconstruction. VMM plus standby has not had a combined full-model
+fault-injection run.
+
+The experiment used driver 580.105.08, CUDA driver API 13.0, Torch 2.13.0+cu130,
+FlashInfer 0.6.18 and sglang-kernel 0.4.7. The frozen source expected kernel 0.4.9;
+its version check was explicitly bypassed. This dependency mismatch is an open
+validation gap, not a recommended deployment configuration.
+
+Full-capacity throughput, speculative/draft execution, other topologies,
+multi-node operation, daemon loss and in-flight state recovery are unvalidated.
+This extension does not implement the parallel checkpoint-read optimization in
+SGLang #42920. Keep this feature experimental until the remaining gates pass.
+
+The CPU contract tests can be run individually:
+
+```bash
+for test in test_host_vmm_weight_cache test_host_engram_weight_cache \
+            test_dsv41_weight_cache_state test_weight_cache_protocol test_warm_standby; do
+  python "test/registered/unit/model_loader/${test}.py"
+done
+```

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Process-local mappings of exportable CUDA HOST_NUMA allocations.
+
+The daemon allocates once. Clients import the CUDA allocation FD and establish
+CPU/GPU access without cudaHostRegister. Tensor users must retire before close.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ctypes
+import logging
+import os
+import time
+
+import torch
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+
+def _checked(result):
+    if int(result[0]) != 0:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"CUDA host VMM operation failed: {result}")
+    return result[1] if len(result) == 2 else result[1:]
+
+
+def _cuda_driver():
+    try:
+        from cuda.bindings import driver
+    except ImportError as error:
+        raise RuntimeError("CUDA host VMM requires cuda.bindings.driver") from error
+    # Establish Torch's current primary context; do not retain a second context.
+    torch.empty(0, device="cuda")
+    return driver, torch.cuda.current_device()
+
+
+class _CudaArrayView:
+    def __init__(self, address, nbytes):
+        self.__cuda_array_interface__ = {
+            "shape": (nbytes,),
+            "typestr": "|u1",
+            "data": (int(address), False),
+            "version": 3,
+        }
+
+
+class HostVmmAllocation:
+    def __init__(self, driver, device):
+        self.driver, self.device = driver, device
+        self.fd = None
+        self.handle = None
+        self.address = None
+        self.mapped = False
+        self.bytes = None
+        self.closed = False
+        self.gpu_view = False
+        self.mapping_timings = {}
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _props(driver, numa_id):
+        prop = driver.CUmemAllocationProp()
+        prop.type = driver.CUmemAllocationType.CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED
+        prop.requestedHandleTypes = (
+            driver.CUmemAllocationHandleType.CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_POSIX_FILE_DESCRIPTOR
+        )
+        prop.location.type = driver.CUmemLocationType.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA
+        prop.location.id = numa_id
+        return prop
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _require_support(driver, device):
+        for name in (
+            "CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_VIRTUAL_MEMORY_MANAGEMENT_SUPPORTED",
+            "CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HANDLE_TYPE_POSIX_FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SUPPORTED",
+        ):
+            attribute = getattr(driver.CUdevice_attribute, name, None)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Experimental post-load state transport for DeepSeek V4.1.
+
+Tensor payloads use the existing IPC transport. The manifest contains only
+references and primitive metadata; no tensors, callables, or CUDA resources.
+Host Engram uses daemon-owned memfds or CUDA HOST_NUMA VMM allocations. Mutable request state is not cached.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import importlib.metadata
+import json
+import os
+
+import torch
+
+STATE_ENTRY = "__sglang_model_state__"
+TENSOR_PREFIX = "__sglang_model_tensor__/"
+CONTRACT = "deepseek_v41_post_load_v3"
+# Post-load flags consumed by the model, rather than purely constructor flags.
+MODULE_FLAGS = (
+    "ape_converted",
+    "_mxfp4_backend",
+    "_mega_moe_weights_built",
+    "block_fp8_mxfp8_ready",
+    "intermediate_size_per_partition",
+    "hidden_pad",
+    "intermediate_pad",
+    "pad_id",
+    "image_token_id",
+    "k_scale_float",
+    "v_scale_float",
+    "use_padded_loading",
+)
+PARAM_FLAGS = ("format_ue8m0",)
+
+
+def is_dsv41(model_config) -> bool:
+    cfg = getattr(model_config, "hf_text_config", model_config.hf_config)
+    return getattr(cfg, "model_type", None) in ("deepseek_v41", "deepseek_v4.1")
+
+
+def model_state_contract(model_config, extra_config) -> str:
+    if not is_dsv41(model_config):
+        return ""
+    if isinstance(extra_config, str):
+        extra_config = json.loads(extra_config)
+    if not isinstance(extra_config or {}, dict):
+        raise ValueError("model-loader-extra-config must be a JSON object")
+    if (extra_config or {}).get("dsv41_weight_cache") is not True:
+        raise ValueError(
+            "DeepSeek V4.1 IPC recovery is experimental; explicitly set "
+            "model-loader-extra-config must contain dsv41_weight_cache=true."
+        )
+    return CONTRACT
+
+
+def host_table_backend(extra_config):
+    if isinstance(extra_config, str):
+        extra_config = json.loads(extra_config)
+    backend = (extra_config or {}).get("dsv41_host_table_backend", "memfd")
+    if backend not in ("memfd", "cuda_vmm"):
+        raise ValueError("dsv41_host_table_backend must be memfd or cuda_vmm")
+    return backend
+
+
+def layout_fingerprint(model_config, server_args) -> str:
+    """Stamp choices that change packed weights or derived model state."""
+    fields = (
+        "moe_runner_backend",
+        "fp8_gemm_runner_backend",
+        "fp4_gemm_runner_backend",
+        "bf16_gemm_backend",
+        "quantization",
+        "enable_shared_experts_fusion",
+        "enable_deterministic_inference",
+        "flashinfer_mxfp4_moe_precision",
+        "enable_symm_mem",
+    )
+    data = {
+        "contract": CONTRACT,
+        "host_backend": host_table_backend(
+            getattr(server_args, "model_loader_extra_config", None)
+        ),
+        "config": model_config.hf_config.to_dict(),
+        "flags": {k: getattr(server_args, k, None) for k in fields},
+        "env": {
+            k: v
+            for k, v in sorted(os.environ.items())
+            if k.startswith(
+                (
+                    "SGLANG_OPT_",
+                    "SGLANG_DSV4",
+                    "SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM",
+                    "SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_",
+                    "SGLANG_MXFP",
+                    "SGLANG_USE_AITER",
+                )
+            )
+        },
+    }
+    libraries = {}
+    for package in (
+        "sglang-kernel",
+        "flashinfer-python",
+        "deep-gemm",
+        "triton",
+        "tvm-ffi",
+        "tilelang",
+    ):
+        try:
+            libraries[package] = importlib.metadata.version(package)
+        except importlib.metadata.PackageNotFoundError:
+            libraries[package] = ""
+    data["libraries"] = libraries
+    # Two checkouts may have the same library version but different weight
+    # transforms. Include source content, not paths, in the identity.
+    from pathlib import Path
+
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    paths = (
+        "weight_cache/model_state.py",
+        "models/deepseek_v4.py",
+        "layers/engram.py",
+        "weight_cache/transport.py",
+        "weight_cache/host_vmm.py",
+        "layers/attention/dsv4/compressor.py",
+        "layers/quantization/fp8.py",
+        "layers/quantization/fp8_utils.py",
+        "layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py",
+        "layers/moe/mega_moe.py",
+    )
+    data["source"] = {
+        p: hashlib.sha256((root / p).read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in paths
+    }
+    return hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(data, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
+
+
+def _primitive(value):
+    if value is None or type(value) in (bool, int, float, str):
+        return True
+    return isinstance(value, (list, tuple)) and all(_primitive(v) for v in value)
+
+
+def _tensor_tree(value):
+    if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+        return True
+    return (
+        isinstance(value, (tuple, list))
+        and bool(value)
+        and all(_tensor_tree(v) or v is None for v in value)
+    )
+
+
+def _class_name(obj):
+    cls = type(obj)
+    return f"{cls.__module__}.{cls.__qualname__}"
+
+
+def export_model_state(model, state_tensors):
+    """Capture derived tensor references and metadata after weight transforms.
+
+    This runs before any request/KV initialization. Module registries and
+    quantization runner objects remain constructed in the client; they are
+    never pickled. Derived tensor trees keep their tuple/list structure.
+    """
+    manifest = {
+        "contract": CONTRACT,
+        "schema": {},
+        "objects": {},
+        "attrs": [],
+        "params": {},
+        "extras": {},
+    }
+    for name, (tensor, is_param) in state_tensors.items():
+        manifest["schema"][name] = [list(tensor.shape), str(tensor.dtype), is_param]
+    tensor_ids = {}
+
+    def encode(value):
+        if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
+            key = tensor_ids.get(id(value))
+            if key is None:
+                key = f"{TENSOR_PREFIX}{len(tensor_ids)}"
+                tensor_ids[id(value)] = key
+                state_tensors[key] = (value.detach(), False)
+                manifest["extras"][key] = [list(value.shape), str(value.dtype)]
+            return {"tensor": key}
+        return {
+            "tuple" if isinstance(value, tuple) else "list": [
+                None if v is None else encode(v) for v in value
+            ]
+        }
+
+    def capture(path, obj, quant=False):
+        manifest["objects"][path] = _class_name(obj)
+        for attr, value in vars(obj).items():
+            if _tensor_tree(value):
+                manifest["attrs"].append([path, attr, encode(value)])
+            elif attr in MODULE_FLAGS or (quant and _primitive(value)):
+                if not _primitive(value):
+                    raise ValueError(f"Non-primitive post-load flag: {path}.{attr}")
+                manifest["attrs"].append([path, attr, {"value": value}])
+
+    for path, module in model.named_modules():
+        capture(path, module)
+        method = getattr(module, "quant_method", None)
+        if method is not None:
+            qpath = f"{path}.quant_method" if path else "quant_method"
+            capture(qpath, method, quant=True)
+            wrapped = getattr(method, "_fp8", None)
+            if wrapped is not None:
+                capture(qpath + "._fp8", wrapped, quant=True)
+    for name, param in model.named_parameters(remove_duplicate=False):
+        flags = {k: getattr(param, k) for k in PARAM_FLAGS if hasattr(param, k)}
+        if flags:
+            manifest["params"][name] = flags
+    return manifest
+
+
+def host_table_exports(model, state_tensors):
+    """Describe registered Engram views without serializing CPU tensor payloads."""
+    entries, fds = {}, []
+    for path, module in model.named_modules():
+        table = getattr(module, "host_table", None)
+        if table is None:
+            continue
+        if table.fd is None:
+            raise ValueError(
+                "IPC host Engram requires daemon-owned shareable host storage"
+            )
+        descriptor = {
+            "index": len(fds),
+            "module": path,
+            "layout": table.layout,
+            "nbytes": table.nbytes,
+        }
+        if getattr(table, "backend", "memfd") == "cuda_vmm":
+            descriptor.update(
+                backend="cuda_vmm",
+                allocation_nbytes=table._vmm.allocation_nbytes,
+                numa_id=table._vmm.numa_id,
+            )
+        fds.append(table.fd)
+        for attr in ("weight", "scale"):
+            name = f"{path}.{attr}"
+            tensor, is_param = state_tensors[name]
+            if tensor.device.type != "cpu" or not tensor.is_contiguous():
+                raise ValueError(f"Invalid host Engram tensor: {name}")
+            entries[name] = {
+                "host_table": descriptor,
+                "host_offset": tensor.data_ptr() - table.bytes.data_ptr(),
+                "shape": list(tensor.shape),
+                "dtype": str(tensor.dtype).replace("torch.", ""),
+                "is_param": is_param,
+            }
+    return entries, fds
+
+
+def _resolve(model, path):
+    obj = model
+    for part in path.split(".") if path else ():
+        obj = getattr(obj, part)
+    return obj
+
+
+def validate_model_state(model, manifest):
+    if manifest.get("contract") != CONTRACT:
+        raise ValueError("Missing or incompatible V4.1 post-load state contract")
+    for path, cls in manifest["objects"].items():
+        if _class_name(_resolve(model, path)) != cls:
+            raise ValueError(f"V4.1 IPC object class mismatch at {path}")
+
+
+def restore_model_state(model, manifest, tensors):
+    validate_model_state(model, manifest)
+
+    def decode(value):
+        if "tensor" in value:
+            return tensors[value["tensor"]]
+        if "value" in value:
+            return value["value"]
+        if "tuple" in value:
+            return tuple(None if v is None else decode(v) for v in value["tuple"])
+        if "list" in value:
+            return [None if v is None else decode(v) for v in value["list"]]
